summary: Quiet long-lived cohort causes intermittent reserved pool attach failures and autoscaler under-provisioning
description:
Issue summary: Production reserved capacity in us-east experienced a gradual throughput sag between 09:10–11:00 UTC on 2026-03-13. The cluster showed sudden attach latency spikes (~600ms p95 -> 2s p99) and transient GPU allocation shortfalls that caused soft 5xx throttles for a subset of customers. Impact: multiple dedicated-tier customers saw request timeouts and degraded p99 latency for short streaming requests.

Impact: 3 enterprise and 5 dedicated customers reported increased error rates and elevated latencies on batched and short-stream routes. No service-wide outage; degradation limited to two reserved pools (rp-us-east-3b, rp-us-east-5c).

Environment: prod | us-east (reserved pools). Affected services: serving-runtime, autoscaler, allocator, kernel-selection.

Steps to reproduce: 
1) Replay traces from the affected pool during 09:10–10:30 UTC.
2) Start a cohort of ~300 long-lived low-throughput connections that send a keepalive every 60s and occasional 1–3 token inference calls.
3) Observe allocator attach latency and autoscaler behavior as synthetic load ramps in bursts.

Observed behaviour: allocator heartbeats report stable capacity but attach operations intermittently fail with timeouts; autoscaler did not add new nodes because connection rate and token throughput were below its threshold. KV cache prefills and small prefix cache growth from the cohort increased per-GPU memory overhead, causing effective slot fragmentation and sporadic rejection of short attach attempts.

Expected behaviour: autoscaler should detect hidden capacity pressure caused by connection + KV cache footprint and either add capacity or surface a graceful fallback earlier. Attach latencies should remain < 250ms p95 for these pools.

Temporary workaround: Enabled tenant-level fallback to a compatible hosted model variant for affected customers and increased reserved-pool attach timeout to 6s for the impacted pools to reduce client-facing 5xx. Scaled up pool rp-us-east-5c by +2 nodes manually during mitigation window.

Customer communication: Notified affected customers via support thread and provided workaround instructions; one enterprise customer requested a postmortem and configuration guidance for long-lived connection patterns.
comments: 2026-03-13 11:25 - Carlos Nguyen (Support): Initial triage: heap and host-level telemetry shows elevated GPU memory utilization patterns inconsistent with request rate. Suspect cache growth from many long-lived connections. Collected heap dumps and allocator traces.

2026-03-13 12:02 - SRE Oncall (Alexei Voronin): Observed periodic KV cache increases on several host processes; one host in rp-us-east-3b hit soft OOM and started rejecting new attachments. Manual scale and attach-timeout bump applied.
2026-03-13 13:40 - Customer (AcmeRetail): We see timeouts for short chatlet requests and occasional 502s. Thanks for the temporary fallback — can you advise best practice for keepalive frequency?

2026-03-13 14:05 - Maya Patel (Support): Recommended keepalive >= 120s for long-lived connections to reduce ephemeral KV churn; provided sample SDK config. Ticket escalated to runtime engineers for tuning autoscaler and KV eviction heuristics.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Runtime Eng (Priya Ramesh): Running targeted experiment in staging to lower autoscaler add thresholds when connection churn is high but token throughput is low. Also prototyping a lightweight footprint sampling to surface hidden per-tenant memory usage to autoscaler.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 09:10 UTC - gradual p99 attach latency increases; 09:30 UTC - first customer report; 09:45 UTC - SRE noticed KV cache step-ups correlated to long-lived sockets; 10:10 UTC - autoscaler did not scale due to rate-based trigger. Hypothesis: a small cohort of long-lived, low QPS streams with periodic prefetches/keepalives is creating a persistent per-connection memory footprint that evades throughput-based autoscaler triggers and produces slot fragmentation on GPUs. Evidence: heap profiles show per-connection cache entries; allocator logs show attach failures preceded by cache growth events; kernel-selection logs indicate degraded packing efficiency.

Interim telemetry queries:
- Query: per-tenant kv_cache_bytes by pool -> shows step ups in specific tenant cohorts.
- Query: attach_latency by host -> correlated with hosts running the cohort.

Mitigations attempted: manual pool scale, attach timeout bump, tenant fallbacks, customer SDK guidance.

Open unknowns: exact KV entry lifecycle for keepalive-triggered prefetches; whether eviction tuning alone is sufficient or autoscaler needs new signal.
resolution_notes:
In progress — temporary mitigations applied and customer fallbacks set. Longer-term work accepted into runtime backlog: 1) Add a memory-footprint signal to autoscaler (PR opened), 2) KV eviction policy tuning to prefer short-lived entries and aggressive aging for keepalive-prefetches, 3) SDK guidance page for long-lived connections.

Immediate outcome: manual scaling and timeout bump removed most 5xxs; p95/p99 latencies returned to baseline for majority of customers by 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC.

Owners: Runtime Eng for autoscaler changes (Priya Ramesh), KV team for eviction policy (Diego Morales), Support for customer follow-ups (Maya Patel).
root_cause: Hidden per-connection KV cache growth from a quiet cohort of long-lived streams produced GPU slot fragmentation and memory pressure that was not visible to a throughput-only autoscaler, leading to attach timeouts and transient GPU allocation shortfalls.
action_items: Autoscaler: implement memory-footprint signal and integrate into scale-up decision path
KV-cache: implement aggressive aging for keepalive-prefetch entries and add metrics for per-connection footprint
Support/Docs: publish long-lived connection best-practices and SDK config recommendations
SRE: schedule reserved-pool soak with synthetic quiet-cohort to validate changes before rollout
